To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the subcellular fractioning of Cd, Pb, and Zn is a useful tool to assess the bioavailability of metals in earthworms; and (2) metallothionein is a reliable and sensitive biomarker in A. caliginosa exposed to field-contamination.

metal subcellular fractionations provide better predictors of biomarker response than the total internal content, and that metallothionein and integrated biomarker indices are the most robust and specific biomarkers in earth-worms exposed to field contaminated soil.
the most soluble pools of metals were often the worst predictors of biomarker response, and that the most insoluble fractions were the best predictors of the biomarker responses.
In summary, our research is concerned with

improving the understanding of the mechanisms involved in metal toxicity to earthworms in field-contaminated sites, and provides useful information to improve biomonitoring of metal-contaminated soils.
the use of subcellular fractioning of metals to better understand the relationships between metal exposure and biomarker responses.

the identification of subcellular metal fractions that are most relevant for the assessment of the toxicological bioavailability and the development of biomarkers of exposure and effect for earthworms exposed in situ to metal-contaminated field soils.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the most soluble internal pools are not always the best indicators of the toxicological pressure on earthworms, and that subcellular fractioning is a useful tool to identify metal fractions which better reflect metal bioavailabilities and toxicity to earthworms.
the most soluble metal fractions are not necessarily the most bioavailable to earthworms.
metal compartmentalization into subcellular fractions is a good predictor of the toxic pressure on earthworms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the toxicological bioavailability to earthworms of Cd and Pb from field-contaminated sites is mainly related to their distribution in the insoluble metal fractions (debris > granules).
metallothionein is a promising biomarker to assess Cd and Pb toxic pressure in A. caliginosa.

metallothioneins are good predictors of metal stress in earthworms, and that subcellular partitioning of metals in the cytosol, debris + granule compartments is a good predictor for biomarker responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the toxicological effects on earthworms exposed in the field to contaminated soils can be predicted from the subcellular metal distribution in the organism.
subcellular fractioning of metals in earthworms is a useful tool to identify metal fractions that are relevant for the assessment of toxic pressure in contaminated soils.

the subcellular distribution of metals in earthworms can be used to predict biomarker responses and thus to better understand the toxicological pressure exerted by metal-contaminated soils on earthworms.
